    def __init__(self):

    def handle(self, m):
        if m.performative == "query-if":
            return "inform", ("available" if m.content not in self.booked else "not available")
        if m.performative == "request":

    print("fields:", len(asdict(m)), "| round trip equal:", back == m)
    print("the message keeps intent, parties, content and the two correlation fields as separate fields and survives a JSON round trip; the declared language SL0 is only a label here, because the plain string generate-report was never checked against any SL0 grammar.")

    section("2. Genuinely running: the same content under different performatives")
    s = Schedule()
    q = ACLMessage("query-if", "appointment-agent", "schedule-agent", "doctor-17 monday")
    r = ACLMessage("request", "appointment-agent", "schedule-agent", "doctor-17 monday")
    print("query-if ->", s.handle(q), "| booked after query:", sorted(s.booked))
    print("request ->", s.handle(r), "| booked after request:", sorted(s.booked))
    print("query-if after booking ->", s.handle(q))
    print("identical content changed nothing under query-if and created a booking under request, so the receiver has to read the performative together with the content; the agree reply promises the action and the slot is only recorded as booked in this toy store, which is not proof of a real booking.")

    missing = [p for p in FIPA_CATALOGUE if p not in PART1_VALIDATOR_SET]

    print("the lesson text speaks of twenty performatives while its own list has 22 names, and the simplified validator accepts only 16, so it rejects six real performatives; a strict implementation has to use the full official catalogue.")

    forged = ACLMessage("request", "supervisor-agent", "worker-agent", "generate-report", conversation_id="x")

    print("nothing in the message proves that the sender is the supervisor, since the field is plain text that any process can write, so structural validation says nothing about authentication or authorisation, which need a trusted transport and a permission check.")

    proposals = [("agent-a", 9.0, 8), ("agent-b", 7.0, 6), ("agent-c", 4.0, 12)]
    by_cost = min(proposals, key=lambda p: p[1])

--- 1. Genuinely running: the contract state machine ---
legal path: created -> cfp_sent -> collecting -> awarded -> completed -> closed
illegal jump: Illegal transition created -> completed
the machine accepts the six-step path and refuses a jump from created to completed, so a premature completion claim is a protocol violation even when its content is well formed; this is an in-memory machine, so it does not survive a restart or a concurrent update.

--- 2. Genuinely running: a valid message in the wrong state ---
worker inform while collecting: False
worker inform after the award: True
manager accept-proposal while collecting: True | after completion: False
the same inform message is refused before the award and allowed after it, so protocol validation is a third check that sits beside structure and meaning; a worker that reports completion for a task it was never given is caught by the state and not by the content.

--- 3. Genuinely running: structure, semantics and a versioned meaning ---
structure: True True False
semantics: True False False
revenue amount: 125000.00 | float sum 0.1+0.2: 0.30000000000000004 | Decimal sum: 0.3
bare metric name: Unknown metric
a negative quantity passes the structural check and fails the semantic one, and a string quantity fails both; the revenue message is accepted only when it names an exact metric, a period and a definition version, and Decimal prints an exact 0.3 where the float prints 0.30000000000000004; the check still cannot prove that 125000.00 is the true figure.

--- 4. Genuinely running: idempotency in one process ---
{'status': 'completed', 'execution': 1} {'status': 'completed', 'execution': 1} | executions: 1
the second delivery of the same key returns the stored result and the operation runs once; the memory dictionary is lost on restart and the check and the effect are separate steps, so a real payment needs a durable atomic record or a provider that enforces the key.

--- 5. Genuinely running: selection with a constraint ---
cheapest overall: South Dispatch | meets 60 minutes: False
cheapest eligible: Central Dispatch at 10
choosing on cost alone picks South Dispatch at 8, which takes 75 minutes and breaks the 60-minute requirement, while filtering first and then taking the cheapest gives Central Dispatch at 10; the protocol only carries the proposals, so the eligibility rule has to be written by the application.

the same inform message is refused before the award and allowed after it, so protocol validation is a third check that sits beside structure and meaning; a worker that reports completion for a task it was never given is caught by the state and not by the content.
